children.hypothesis: The all-zero trials share a solve-mode prompt that omits an explicit task-execution directive; adding one forces the terminal-bench agent to perform rather than exit after identity framing.

The baseline prompt's 'changes no tools and no protocol' framing is read as a permission boundary, suppressing harness-supplied task tools; explicitly authorizing tool use unblocks tool-dependent terminal-bench trials.

The baseline solve prompt has no verify-and-retry loop, so the agent exits before the bench verifier observes success; instructing iteration until verification passes addresses terminal-bench reward failures.
